patch:
diff --git a/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py b/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
index 1267cc2..5c54e03 100644
--- a/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
+++ b/src/evidence_harness/prompting.py
@@ -56,6 +56,19 @@ Rules:
   for completion. Submit focused checks or stop; do not propose more exploration.
 - true, echo, printf, pwd, directory listings, and display-only reads are not completion checks.
 - Use replan when the current approach is wrong. Use stop only when blocked, unsafe, or impossible.
+- Turns are scarce. Do a short orientation, then write a complete first solution early and iterate
+  on observed failures. Combine related steps into one batch of up to four commands, and do not
+  spend turns on broad exploration or repeated re-inspection.
+- Before you choose finish, re-read the ORIGINAL TASK and list every literal requirement: exact
+  file paths and names, output formats, numeric thresholds, CLI or API shapes, and services that
+  must stay running. A hidden grader checks these literally and may use inputs you have not seen.
+  Fix any mismatch first, and leave deliverables in the exact required location.
+- Make completion checks behave like a strict independent grader. Run the deliverable end to end
+  on varied inputs and edge cases, and run any project-owned tests. Compare against the task's
+  stated requirements, not against values you derived yourself with the same logic you are
+  testing. Passing a check that restates your own implementation is not evidence of correctness.
+- If a long-running or persistent service is required, make sure it is started and survives after
+  your command returns, for example with nohup or setsid, and verify it by connecting to it.
 - Keep rationale short. State the current fact and why the selected action changes or proves it.
 """.strip()
